markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests InSitu (66%)** · Unreliable input · Defer to expert
Image looks atypical and three classes stay in the set [F6].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | InSitu 66%, Benign 21%, Invasive 7% | Leading class, not dominant |
| Conformal set | Benign, InSitu, Invasive | Three classes not separable |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.10 / 98th percentile | Input suspect, atypical image |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Different top class |
| Similar cases | 4 of 5 InSitu [F5] | Supports InSitu suggestion |

## Tissue evidence
- **Frequent mitotic figures** (regions 0, 1, 4) · ↑ invasive · Highest concept score above typical; spot check 0/20 [F2] · Unreliable
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 9, 10, 11) · ↓ invasive · Glandular pattern linked to lower invasive likelihood [F3] · Weak
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 0, 1) · ↑ invasive · Above typical, but spot check 3/20 [F4] · Unreliable
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (regions 2, 6) · ↓ invasive · Scored above typical; spot check 12/20 · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI spans 0 (−0.005 to 0.007); not shown to reflect the classifier. Mitoses and necrosis are Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Image is out of distribution (98th percentile, reliability 0.10), so all probabilities are suspect.
- MUSK picks a different top class, so the InSitu call may not hold.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 0, 1:** highest invasive contribution on heatmap; look for invasion, necrosis, mitoses.
2. **Regions 2, 6:** confirm atypia stays within ducts rather than invading stroma.
3. **Regions 9, 10:** confirm benign glands; heatmap shows the strongest push away from invasive.
